theme: Code-health defects and their look-alikes in a parcel shipping rates & label service

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: ComputeSurcharges decides every surcharge in one method: nested branches per carrier, service level, zone, parcel shape and declared value, with compound conditions. Well over any reasonable decision-point budget, and the branches are genuinely distinct paths that each need a test.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The same method nests its branches four levels deep (carrier -> service level -> zone -> parcel shape) with flag variables and early continues: a reader has to hold the whole decision tree to change one surcharge.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: LabelService parses label requests, validates addresses, prices the shipment, picks a carrier, renders the label, writes files and an index to disk, sends the customer e-mail over SMTP and keeps statistics: more than thirty methods and several hundred lines spanning at least five unrelated responsibilities. The whole class is the site.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Render builds the whole ZPL label - header, sender, recipient, routing block, barcodes, service box, customs box and footer - in one method of well over a hundred statement lines, with no extracted sections.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The same Render method compiles to far more IL than a method should (hundreds of instructions of inlined StringBuilder calls and string formatting); it is the largest authored method in the repository.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: AlderParcelAdapter's request building and response mapping were copied from CorvidCourierAdapter and only the endpoint and field names were edited; the two copies have already drifted (one rounds weights, one does not). Shared logic belongs in one place.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The same label-file predicate (extension test plus existence check) is spelled out identically in LabelArchive and in the CLI's print command; when the accepted extensions change, one copy will be missed.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: CarrierAccountManager holds four unrelated groups of state and behaviour - account credentials rotation, a rate-limit counter, an audit trail and a webhook signing secret - whose methods share no fields and never call each other. It is four classes in one.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A TODO comment recording known unfinished work (multi-piece shipments are quoted as single parcels).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A HACK comment marking a known workaround (label numbers padded to satisfy one carrier's validator) left in the shared path.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A file-wide '#pragma warning disable CS8618' with no restore and no reason silences the compiler's uninitialised-non-nullable warning for the whole file; the properties it hides really are null after deserialising an old index entry.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A block of commented-out code (the previous label-number scheme) left in the method that replaced it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Sending the label e-mail is wrapped in a bare catch with an empty body: an SMTP failure is discarded without a log line, so a customer silently never receives their label.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A private method nothing calls (the pre-registry carrier-code normaliser).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A conditional-compilation branch on a symbol no project, build configuration or file defines: its code can never compile or run.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The switch subject is carrierCode.ToUpperInvariant(), so the lower-case label 'alder' can never match; that branch is dead and Alder codes fall through to the default.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Quote is marked [Obsolete] in favour of QuoteParcel, yet LabelService still calls it, so the deprecation announces a removal that the codebase itself blocks.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: VoidLabelAsync is part of the carrier contract the API exposes, and for Corvid it only throws NotImplementedException: voiding a Corvid label fails at run time.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: IsRemoteArea ignores its postal code and returns false, so the remote-area surcharge the calculator asks about is never applied: a hollow stub in a pricing path.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A test skipped with 'fails on CI' - no issue, no category, no condition for re-enabling it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A catch clause whose only statement is 'throw;' - it adds nothing and reads as if handling were intended.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: 'throw ex;' rethrows the caught IOException object, restarting its stack trace at the rethrow and hiding where the write actually failed.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The GET label endpoint blocks a request thread on an async file read with .Result, starving the thread pool under load.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A synchronous Save wrapper blocks on SaveAsync with GetAwaiter().GetResult(); it is called from the request path through LabelService.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: WarmUp is an 'async void' method called at start-up, not an event handler: a failed download crashes the process or is lost, and the caller cannot await completion.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: DownloadAsync performs HTTP I/O and neither accepts nor forwards a CancellationToken, so a shutdown or an aborted request cannot stop it.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A log call whose message is an interpolated string with runtime values, defeating structured logging (the carrier code and count are baked into the text, not captured as properties).

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Shipping.Rates.Tools project sets <Nullable>disable</Nullable>, so the CLI compiles without nullable reference type analysis while every other project has it on. Repository-level: the property is a project posture, reported without a line.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: LabelService silences the nullable analysis with '!' on values that really can be null: a FirstOrDefault carrier lookup (an unknown carrier code), a missing address returned as null!, an optional e-mail stored in a non-nullable property and an index lookup. Repository-level: suppression density is reported without a line.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: RunAsync reads printerName?.Trim() - treating the printer name as possibly null, which it is whenever the optional [printer] argument is omitted - and then dereferences printerName.Length unguarded, so 'print <file>' without a printer throws NullReferenceException instead of using the default printer.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Alder error body is JSON and the project already parses JSON with System.Text.Json, yet the error code is pulled out with a regular expression that breaks on whitespace, escaping or field order.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: When Corvid's transit-days field does not parse, the quote silently promises 3 days: no log, no signal to the caller, and the customer sees an invented delivery date.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The printer process is started with both stdout and stderr redirected, but only stdout is read (ReadToEnd); a chatty stderr fills the pipe buffer and both processes deadlock.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: FitToWidth drops the last character while the measured width exceeds the field; the measure includes fixed margins, so for a narrow field the loop consumes the whole string and Substring throws on the empty string.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: RateCardCache creates its refresh Timer and implements IDisposable, but Dispose never disposes the timer, so refreshes keep firing against a disposed cache.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Run changes the process working directory and restores it only on the success path; an exception while importing leaves the whole process in the wrong directory.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The guard throws ArgumentNullException for an EMPTY (non-null) parcel list as well, misreporting the cause to the caller.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The case guard increments the 'oversize' counter inside the '&&' chain: it is skipped entirely for Economy and runs for every parcel, oversize or not, otherwise - so a third parcel that is oversize is rejected even when it is the only oversize one.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: TryReserveSlotAsync returns true (slot held) on a path where the finally block still releases the semaphore, so the caller believes it holds a slot it no longer has.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: A debug log call materialises every quote into a joined string on every request, whether or not debug logging is enabled.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The constructor stores the configured TTL (with a 30-minute fallback) in a field nothing reads; the staleness check re-spells the 30-minute default, so configuring the TTL has no effect.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: FileSystemWatcher raises Created on thread-pool threads; the handler adds to a plain List that the waiting loop reads concurrently without a lock.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The loop removes over-limit quotes from the List it is enumerating, which throws InvalidOperationException on the next iteration.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The condition guards value[0] with value.Length > 0 on one side of '||' but indexes value[0] again on the other, unguarded: an empty tracking number throws IndexOutOfRangeException.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Inside the per-parcel loop the dangerous-goods surcharge is decided by parcels[0], not parcels[i]: every parcel is charged (or not) according to the first one.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The insurance guard negates 'supports insurance || insured value != 0'; the '!=' has the wrong polarity, so for a carrier without insurance it rejects uninsured shipments and offers insured ones. Dormant with today's two carriers (both insure), live for any partner adapter that does not.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: Custom adapters are resolved by scanning every type of every loaded assembly for a simple-name match: ambiguous when two assemblies define the name, and slow.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: value.StartsWith("JJD00") is implied by value.StartsWith("JJD") in the same '||' chain, so the operand can never change the result - it was meant to distinguish a variant and does not.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The Core project demotes CS0618 (use of an obsolete member) and CA2200 (rethrow resets the stack trace) from errors to warnings, project-wide and without a reason, instead of fixing the two sites that raise them (CH-017's caller, CH-022). Every future occurrence of either defect now builds green.

entries.label: must-fire
entries.rationale: The _ttl field is assigned in the constructor and read nowhere: dead state. It is the same defect as CH-041 (the inert TTL option) seen as unused code; added after scan iteration 1 showed the key had missed that a write-only field is, in itself, unused code.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A flat switch that maps (carrier, service level) to the carrier's product code: many case labels, so a decision-point count is high, but every arm is a one-line return with no nesting or interaction. A reviewer reads it as a lookup table, not as complex logic; splitting it would make it worse.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated code: the file carries an <auto-generated> header and [GeneratedCode], and is regenerated from the rate-card CSV by tools/generate-zones.py. Its size, its one large switch and its single long method are the generator's output; nobody edits or reviews it by hand.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated code: the file carries an <auto-generated> header and [GeneratedCode], and is regenerated from the rate-card CSV by tools/generate-zones.py. Its size, its one large switch and its single long method are the generator's output; nobody edits or reviews it by hand.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated code: the file carries an <auto-generated> header and [GeneratedCode], and is regenerated from the rate-card CSV by tools/generate-zones.py. Its size, its one large switch and its single long method are the generator's output; nobody edits or reviews it by hand.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated code: the file carries an <auto-generated> header and [GeneratedCode], and is regenerated from the rate-card CSV by tools/generate-zones.py. Its size, its one large switch and its single long method are the generator's output; nobody edits or reviews it by hand.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Generated code ([GeneratedCode] on the type): its two switch methods compile to thousands of IL instructions each, by construction of a 249-row lookup. Nobody maintains that IL; measuring it as authored code is wrong.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The field holding the refresh Timer is never read, but it is not dead: a System.Threading.Timer that nothing references is eligible for garbage collection and stops firing, so the field is what keeps the timer alive. (Its missing disposal is CH-035, a different concept.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: ExtractErrorCode returns the sentinel "UNKNOWN" only on an error path: its result is always logged with the HTTP status and thrown inside a CarrierException, so nothing is silent and no default masquerades as data. (The regex itself is CH-031.)

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Intentional duplication across bounded contexts: the public API's address contract and Alder's wire format have the same fields today but change for different reasons and on different schedules. Sharing one type would couple the API to a carrier. Data-only records, no logic.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The other half of the intentional DTO pair (TRP-006): Alder's wire record, owned by the carrier adapter.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The catch logs the failure with the label id and path and then rethrows with 'throw;': it adds context the exception lacks and preserves the stack trace. Not pointless.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A bare 'throw;' rethrows in place and keeps the original stack trace.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An event handler (object sender, FileSystemEventArgs e) for FileSystemWatcher.Changed: async void is the only signature an event accepts, and the body catches and logs every exception so nothing escapes.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Opting in to an API the library marks [Experimental("SHIPRATES001")]: a disable/restore pair around the one statement that uses it, with the reason in the two comment lines above. Suppressing an experimental-API diagnostic at the call site is the documented way to opt in.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: "TODO" is a status code in Corvid's tracking API (a shipment not yet collected), inside a string literal; it is data, not a debt comment.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: The static Main of a console tool waits for its one async command with GetAwaiter().GetResult(). A console process has no synchronisation context and nothing else to do; blocking the main thread until the work ends is what an entry point does, with no deadlock or starvation risk.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Many small methods, all reading the same rate table and options: one responsibility (surcharge rules), every method connected through shared state. Many methods is not low cohesion.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A narrow catch of FileNotFoundException with a comment explaining why ignoring it is correct (the file was replaced again before it could be read; the next Changed event reloads it).

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An interpolated message whose only hole is a const string: it compiles to a constant template, so nothing structured is lost.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Repository-level: the libraries are application code hosted only by ASP.NET Core and a console tool, neither of which installs a synchronisation context; nothing is published as a package. ConfigureAwait(false) would change nothing.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Validate changes the working directory and restores it in a finally block: restored on every path.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Removing from a Dictionary while enumerating its Keys is supported since .NET Core 3.0 (Remove does not invalidate the enumerator); the project targets net10.0.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: 'value.Length == 0 || value[0] == ...' - the index is only evaluated when the length test failed, so it is covered by its own guard.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A truncation loop with a floor: the condition stops at the empty string.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Both streams are redirected and both are drained (stderr asynchronously via BeginErrorReadLine, stdout with ReadToEnd): no deadlock.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A switch on code.ToUpperInvariant() whose labels are upper case: every label can match.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: A regular expression validating the shape of a tracking number - not a structured format with a parser.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: An unparsable configured cut-off time falls back to the documented default AND logs a warning naming the bad value: not silent.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Alder Parcel does not collect parcels (they are handed in at a service point, and Capabilities says SupportsPickup: false); refusing SchedulePickupAsync with NotSupportedException and a message is the complete, correct implementation of that contract member, not a stub.

entries.label: must-not-fire
entries.rationale: Same site as TRP-026: a deliberate capability refusal, not a NotImplementedException placeholder.

entries.label: not-applicable
entries.rationale: A server-side rating service and console tool: no Blazor components, no JavaScript and no JS interop calls anywhere in the repository.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One genuinely over-complex method (CH-001) among roughly two hundred small ones: a real but bounded deduction. Not 100, because the defect is real; not low, because it is one method.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Same reasoning as BND-001 for the nested decision tree in CH-002; the flat mapping switch (TRP-001) adds none.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One copy-pasted pair of carrier adapter members (CH-006) in a ~2-3 kLoC codebase: a small density of clones.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One low-cohesion class (CH-008) among a few dozen cohesive ones.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: One oversized method (CH-005) among a few hundred compact ones.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: A line-of-business service that uses no spans, pools or value tasks, and has no hot path that would need them: low allocation awareness, which is appropriate here, so the band sits at the bottom of the scale's range.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: Mostly idiomatic .NET naming, but the messy legacy parts mix styles (snake_case locals, Hungarian-style prefixes, abbreviations such as 'calc', 'tmp', 'cc'). Judged by a model on a sample: wide band.

entries.label: score-band
entries.rationale: The clean parts carry few, purposeful comments; the messy parts have comments that restate the code ('// increment the counter') and one that is stale. Judged by a model on a sample: wide band.
